info.title: Dietary Supplement Label and Nutrient Intake Analysis
info.description: Look up dietary supplement labels from the NIH Dietary Supplement Label Database (DSLD) and total vitamin and mineral intake across a list of supplements, compared with NIH recommended amounts (RDA/AI) and upper limits (UL). Information only, not medical advice; see the terms of use: https://github.com/chariot-ventures/dietary-supplement-analysis/blob/main/TERMS.md

post.description: Searches the NIH DSLD and returns up to `limit` (max 10) product summaries. On-market only by default.

dedupe_versions.description: Collapse label versions of the same product (same brand and name) into one result, newest first; older IDs are listed in other_versions

search_source.description: "local" when NIH DSLD was unreachable and results came from the service's own label store

post.summary: FDA recalls and adverse event reports
post.description: Recalls (openFDA food enforcement reports, which cover dietary supplements) and CAERS adverse event reports for one product, given as a DSLD ID, barcode, name, or brand and name. A recall is listed only when its description carries the product's barcode or the brand and every distinctive product-name word; others mentioning the brand are counted. Adverse event reports are counted for the product (brand and name words) or, failing that, the brand. A report does not show that the product caused the event.

post.description: Per-nutrient daily totals across 1-15 products (product names, barcodes, DSLD IDs or custom ingredient lists), compared with upper limits and reference intakes when age and sex are given. Returns a plain-language agent_summary, how each named product was identified, single-product changes that would bring above-UL nutrients under the UL, and (with candidates) the effect of adding each candidate. No flag means nothing to report, not a judgement about the stack.

life_stage.description: Pregnancy or lactation (breastfeeding) reference values; requires sex "female" and age 14-50

conditions.description: Conditions that change how NIH reads a dose: smoker (current or former, or asbestos exposure: beta-carotene), kidney_disease (potassium, magnesium, phosphorus), hemochromatosis (iron, vitamin C), lab_test_soon (biotin interferes with lab tests), cancer_treatment (antioxidant doses)

candidates.description: Optional, up to 5: products the user is considering adding. Each is evaluated as an addition to the stack in candidate_results[]; they are not included in nutrient_totals.

detail.description: Present only with "detail": "summary": the response then has profile, summary, agent_summary, resolutions, flagged, suggestions, candidate_results, data_gap_codes and provenance

agent_summary.description: Plain sentences summarizing the result, ready to relay as written; in Spanish with "lang": "es"

flagged.description: detail=summary only: flagged nutrients with amount, UL, percent, severity and UL basis

provenance.description: Code version, git commit and reference-data review date behind this answer; full detail at GET /v1/provenance

resolutions.description: Present when any product was given as {query} or {upc}

timing.description: NIH ODS timing statements that apply to this stack (calcium dose size and form, calcium and iron, iron and zinc, iron with food, vitamin D with fat, green tea extract with food, and medication timing for in-stack interactions): id, nutrient_ids, product_refs, advice, advice_es, source. Summary form: the advice strings, in Spanish with "lang": "es".

foods.description: Present with "foods": source (USDA SR28), items (how each food was matched: ndb_number, description, confidence, grams, portion used, alternatives, nutrients not analyzed) and totals (per nutrient from the foods; food-only nutrients carry percent_of_ul and flags). Supplement totals with the foods added are in nutrient_totals[].with_foods.

botanicals.description: Present when the stack contains a botanical or other non-nutrient ingredient with an NIH NCCIH/ODS safety signal (ashwagandha, kava, St. John's wort, ginkgo, green tea extract, turmeric, black cohosh, garcinia, red yeast rice, goldenseal, berberine, yohimbe, ephedra, valerian, echinacea, garlic, Asian ginseng, saw palmetto, milk thistle, licorice root, bitter orange, fenugreek, cinnamon, creatine). Matched exactly on the DSLD ingredient group or name. Each has signals (kind, summary), the pregnancy statement, dose_findings (creatine, EGCG, valerian amounts against cited doses) and the source. Summary form: id, name, product_refs, signal, dose.

interactions.description: Present when medications or conditions were given. Full form: scope, reviewed, medications (how each name was matched) and findings (all NIH-listed interactions, those involving nutrients in the stack first). Summary form: medications, in-stack findings, and a not_in_stack count.

get.description: Service version, git commit (link to the exact source), and the edition or review date of each data source.
Every operation as {name, path, description, input_schema} (JSON Schema). Call them via their path or POST /v1/tool.
Markdown guide (the same text as llms.txt in the repository) inside a JSON object.

post.description: MCP-style call: {"tool": "stack_analyze", "arguments": {...}}. Returns the same body as the matching route.

tool.description: Which tool to run. Defaults to stack_analyze

name.description: Same as tool (the MCP tools/call field name)

arguments.description: The tool's input, as in GET /v1/tools

via.description: "rxnorm": the name was normalized to its ingredient with NIH RxNav

trigger.description: The medication as given, or the condition id

botanical_ids.description: Botanicals involved, for botanical-medication interactions (St. John's wort, ginkgo, kava...)

in_stack.description: True when the stack supplies one of the nutrients (condition findings: at or above the checked dose)

check.description: DATA_SUSPECT only: which consistency check on the DSLD record failed

per_serving.description: Per serving in the nutrient canonical unit; null if missing or not convertible

entry_date.description: Date this label version was entered into DSLD

other_versions.description: DSLD IDs of older versions of the same product

ul_basis.description: What the UL protects against (the critical adverse effect it is based on)

complete.description: False when some label rows could not be counted; the total is then a lower bound

amount_toward_ul.description: The part of the total the UL applies to (e.g. folic acid, preformed vitamin A)

coverage.description: Percent of the RDA (or AI) supplied by these supplements alone. Informational: diet normally supplies the rest

flags.description: above_ul: the amount the UL applies to exceeds it. near_ul: 90-100% of the UL. No flag means nothing to report

severity.description: high: 2x the UL or more; moderate: above the UL; low: within 10% of the UL

Resolution.description: How a {query} or {upc} product was identified

Suggestion.description: A single-product change and its arithmetic effect on an above-UL nutrient

resolves.description: True when this change alone brings the amount to or under the UL

CandidateResult.description: Effect of adding one candidate product to the stack
